//: TYPECHECKING FOR THE FILE THAT RENDERS THE SECURITY DECISIONS.
media/main.js is 1,776 lines -- 28% of this extension -- and until
2026-09-02 it had no static analysis of any kind: it sits outside the root
tsconfig's `include`, so tsc never saw it, and there was no ESLint config
That is where the approval panel lives. On 2026-09-02 the panel was found
to branch on `req.confined` alone and never read `req.reaches_network`, so
a VS Code user approving web_search was shown the third-party subprocess
warning instead of being told their words were leaving the machine. The
wire type had never declared the field either. A field-name typo in this
file fails silently at runtime and nothing could flag it.
checkJs is the smallest control that would have caught the type half.
strict is deliberately NOT enabled here: this is a browser script written
without annotations, and turning on strict null checks would produce
hundreds of findings on day one, which is how a gate gets switched off.
The bar is 'no undefined symbols, no wrong arity, no obvious type errors',
and it can be raised once it is green and staying green.
